title: GPU-less first run cannot reach RunPod - the local engine install modal has no escape hatch
description: Surfaced 2026-07-29 while fixing MPI-387 F2, and it is a DIFFERENT defect: F2 is which engine build gets picked, this is that the remote escape hatch is unreachable at the moment it is needed. The remote-only boot path already exists and skips the local engine gate (js/shell.js:251, with the intent spelled out in the comment at :244-250), but it is gated on autoConnectOnStart, which defaults to false (js/core/storage.js:61). So a fresh machine takes the local branch, needsInstall is true, and MpiEngineInstall shows with backdropClose:false and no skip or cancel control (MpiEngineInstall.js:322-330) - only engine:ready hides it. The only UI that sets autoConnectOnStart is RunPod settings, behind the landing page the modal is covering. Net effect: a machine with no usable GPU must complete a multi-GB CUDA engine install it will never use, purely to reach the setting that would have let it skip that install. Not a hard block (the CUDA portable installs and ComfyUI falls back to CPU) but a tax on exactly the users RunPod exists for. Needs a product/UX decision before any code - where the escape hatch lives, whether it is always shown or only on gpu.vendor null, the copy, and whether autoConnectOnStart is the right flag or a separate skip-local-engine preference is cleaner. Full trace with file:line evidence in brief.md.
acceptance: A machine with no usable GPU can configure RunPod and generate WITHOUT completing a local ComfyUI engine install
The chosen escape hatch is reachable from the blocking install modal itself, not only from settings behind it
It is decided and written down whether the hatch shows always or only when GPU detection found no discrete GPU
Turning remote back off re-arms the local engine install rather than leaving the app in a half-configured state
